plan: This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, determined by the ascending clock exit points. In such mechanisms, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy—it neither costs you when you'd lose anyway (bidding higher just risks overpaying) nor forgoes profitable wins (bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities). Since my value is $31, I will bid exactly that amount to maximize expected profit.

This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my own bid only determines when I exit, not what I pay if I win. Therefore, bidding my true value ($31) is the dominant strategy—it maximizes my expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher risks winning at a price above my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities.

Since the payment rule is equivalent to a second-price auction (winner pays the second-highest sealed bid), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding below my value risks losing profitable auctions unnecessarily, while bidding above risks overpaying. With a value of $46, I should bid exactly $46 to maximize expected profit.
